title: Any Thoughtful, Informed Response to AI = Better Than a Mindless One
author: Dave Stuart Jr.
summary: Reflecting on his "Let's Talk AI" workshop, Dave Stuart Jr. shares three concrete classroom experiments he ran with AI during the school year: an AI Literacy Kickoff lesson built around an AI-generated article of the week, a one-week trial using Claude to score and give feedback on student essays during writing bootcamp, and repeated use of Claude to analyze class sets of provisional writing for patterns and concerning comments. From these experiments he arrives at a governing principle — that he can respect any teacher's or school's stance on AI, whether zero-AI, mixed-AI, or all-AI, as long as the stance is thoughtful rather than reactive. He defines "thoughtful" specifically: being knowledgeable about the technology's actual capabilities and drawbacks, understanding how learning and motivation genuinely work, and staying serious about educators' unique responsibility for students' long-term flourishing amid rapid technological change. The piece functions as both a practical AI-in-the-classroom field report and an argument that the content of a teacher's AI policy matters less than the rigor of the thinking behind it.
points: Stuart used Claude to score and give feedback on three sets of student essays during writing bootcamp — a use case he flags himself as sounding "crazy" but treats as a genuine data point.
He also used Claude to analyze class sets of provisional writing for patterns and concerning comments, tying the practice back to the Pyramid of Writing Priorities framework from These 6 Things.
His central claim is that any AI stance — zero-AI, mixed-AI, or all-AI — deserves respect as long as it's thoughtful, reframing the debate away from which policy is "right."

He operationalizes "thoughtful" into three testable components: technical knowledge of AI's real capabilities, understanding of how learning and motivation work, and seriousness about teachers' role in students' long-term flourishing.
The AI Literacy Kickoff lesson, built around an AI-generated article of the week, is offered as his flagship classroom example of frank, direct student engagement with AI.
quotes: A one-week experiment during my writing bootcamp in which I used Claude to score and give feedback on three sets of student essays (I know, it sounds crazy).
But here is where I basically landed: at this point in the journey, I can respect any teacher or school response to AI so long as it is thoughtful.
Knowledgable about the state of the technology today, how it works, what it's capable of, what its drawbacks are. Knowledgable about how learning (growth toward mastery) and motivation work.
That said, wherever you fall on the spectrum — zero-AI, mixed-AI, all-AI — I think your students will be better off for having you as a teacher in the years to come.

It's about thoughtful engagement with not just the technology but also its ramifications for learning, motivation, and long-term flourishing. The more people like this we can get in front of our students in the years to come, the better.
